purpose: R33 verification (Codex R32-review mainline) of the ACTUAL production-trainer loader rank behavior, to decide whether the R32 gloo-dump 'both loaders rank-replicated (effective batch 32)' holds for the production nccl runs -- i.e. whether the r22-vs-r24 gap is an effective-batch difference (reference 256 vs RLinf 32) or not.
method: Read the REAL loader-setup code of both production trainers + confirm with the R32 8-rank torchrun dump (num_workers=0 control vs num_workers=8 production).

rlinf_production.worker_init_fn: _worker_init_fn is a no-op placeholder (`del worker_id`, line 170-173) -- does NOT re-establish torch.distributed in the worker
rlinf_production.rank_source: BehaviorSftDataset._select_streaming_chunk reads `dist.get_rank() if dist.is_available() and dist.is_initialized() else 0`
rlinf_production.conclusion: SPAWN workers are fresh interpreters that do NOT inherit the parent's torch.distributed state, so dist.is_initialized() is False in the worker -> the dataset reads rank=0/world_size=1 in ALL ranks' workers -> all ranks replicate rank-0's partition -> RANK-REPLICATED (effective batch = micro_batch_size = 32, NOT the configured global_batch_size 256).

reference_production.shuffle_seed: generator seeded with process_seed = config.seed; `process_seed += jax.process_index()` ONLY when framework=='jax', but create_behavior_data_loader_torch uses framework='pytorch', so process_seed = config.seed -- the SAME generator seed on every rank (no rank/process offset)
reference_production.sampler: sampler=None (no DistributedSampler); local_batch_size = config.batch_size // world_size = 256//8 = 32 per rank
reference_production.worker_init_fn: _worker_init_fn only sets XLA env vars (data_loader.py:421-426) -- does NOT shard by rank
reference_production.conclusion: SPAWN workers + the SAME generator seed across all ranks + no rank-aware sampler -> every rank shuffles the same dataset identically -> RANK-REPLICATED (effective batch = local_batch_size = 32, NOT global 256).

empirical_confirmation_R32: The R32 8-rank torchrun dump directly ran BOTH loaders: at num_workers=8 BOTH are rank-replicated (32 unique frames/global step); the num_workers=0 control is rank-disjoint (256) -- confirming the spawn-worker mechanism (workers lose the dist rank). See docs/evidence/r32_loader_topology.json + r32_*_topology_hashes.json.
verdict: [SUPERSEDED BY R34 -- the reference half is WRONG; see CORRECTION_R34] BOTH production trainers are RANK-REPLICATED (effective per-step batch = 32, not the configured global 256) -- code-confirmed (both use spawn DataLoader workers that do not inherit torch.distributed; the reference additionally uses the SAME shuffle seed across ranks since framework='pytorch' skips the jax.process_index offset) AND dump-confirmed (R32). So the r22-vs-r24 production gap (0.046 vs 0.090) is NOT an effective-batch-size difference -- BOTH are effective batch 32. The R30/R31 loader-composition hypothesis stays REFUTED (R32: same rank-0 frames at seed 42). REMAINING LEADS (R34, unproven): (a) DATA ORDERING -- RLinf production seed=42 vs the reference production's config.seed (if different, the two runs shuffle the same corpus differently); R24 showed the reference reproducible across seeds (~0.004), so this is unlikely to explain ~0.044 alone; (b) the noise/time RNG; (c) a 50-step / effective-batch-32 residual that R28's 20-step single-GPU same-input test did not capture. The r22-vs-r24 gap is genuinely re-opened; task15 NOT met.
caveat: The code reading + R32 gloo dump establish the rank-replication mechanism (spawn workers). The production runs use nccl, but spawn-vs-fork worker behavior is backend-independent (a spawned worker never inherits the parent process group regardless of nccl/gloo), so the mechanism holds. Distinguished: OBSERVED = the dump + the code; INFERRED = the production nccl runs share the spawn mechanism (high-confidence, since both trainers' loader code uses spawn).
CORRECTION_R34: The reference conclusion below is WRONG (Codex R33 review): it modeled each rank independently building create_behavior_data_loader_torch, but train_pytorch_new.py builds the loader on rank 0 ONLY and fans out SUCCESSIVE micro-batches to each rank (rank-DISJOINT, effective batch 256, measured in docs/evidence/r34_production_batch_topology.json). So the reference is effective batch 256, NOT 32, and the r22-vs-r24 gap IS an effective-batch difference (reference 256 vs RLinf's rank-replicated 32). The RLinf-side analysis (spawn workers -> rank-replicated 32) is correct. Superseded by R34.
